title: Find Target Indices After Sorting Array
summary: Find all target indices after sorting the array in non-decreasing order.
approach: Count elements strictly smaller than target (less) and elements equal to target (equal). Target indices in the sorted array are precisely less to less + equal - 1.

title: Number of Ways to Reorder Array to Get Same BST
summary: Find the number of ways to reorder an array such that the constructed BST is identical to the one formed by the original array modulo 10^9 + 7.
approach: Identify root as first element, divide remainder into left and right subtrees. Count interleavings via combinations C(L+R, L) multiplied by recursive subtree ways, subtracting 1 for original permutation.

title: Minimum Swaps to Sort by Digit Sum
summary: Find the minimum number of swaps to sort an array by digit sums (and numerical values on ties) using permutation cycle decomposition.
approach: Compute digit sums for each element, sort indices by (digit_sum, value) to find target positions, and decompose the permutation into disjoint cycles. Each cycle of length K requires K - 1 swaps.

title: Subarrays Distinct Element Sum of Squares II
summary: Compute the sum of squares of distinct element counts across all subarrays modulo 10^9 + 7 using a lazy segment tree.
approach: Maintain distinct counts f(i, j) as j increases using a segment tree. Increment values for starting indices in (last[nums[j]], j] by 1 and query the sum of squares at each step.

title: Subarrays Distinct Element Sum of Squares I
summary: Compute the sum of squares of distinct element counts across all subarrays of nums using an incremental hash set per start index.
approach: Iterate through each starting index i and incrementally add elements nums[j] to a hash set for j >= i. Add the square of the set size to the running total.

title: Maximize Sum of Squares of Digits
summary: Find the good integer of length num with digit sum equal to sum that achieves the maximum sum of digit squares, choosing the largest number in case of ties.
approach: Return empty string if sum > 9 * num. By convexity of x^2, greedily place as many 9s as possible from the highest place value, followed by the remainder digit, and then 0s.

title: Maximum Alternating Sum of Squares
summary: Maximize the alternating sum of squares by greedily assigning the smallest squares to subtracted odd positions and the largest squares to added even positions.
approach: Compute squares of all elements, sort them in ascending order. Assign the smallest n // 2 squares with negative signs and the remaining larger squares with positive signs.

title: Apply Operations on Array to Maximize Sum of Squares
summary: Maximize sum of squares of k elements after applying bitwise AND/OR operations by greedily concentrating conserved set bits into the largest possible numbers.
approach: Total set bits at each position are invariant under AND/OR. Count bits at positions 0..29, greedily construct k numbers with all available bits, and sum squares modulo 10^9 + 7.
timeComplexity: O(N + K) where N = nums.length, K = k

title: Sum of Squares of Special Elements
summary: Calculate the sum of squares of special elements in a 1-indexed array where index i divides the length of the array n.
approach: Iterate i from 1 to n. If n % i == 0, square nums[i - 1] and add to the running sum. Runs in O(N) time with O(1) auxiliary space.

title: Minimum Sum of Squared Difference
summary: Minimize the sum of squared difference by greedily reducing largest absolute differences first using a frequency bucket array.
approach: Pool total reductions k = k1 + k2. Since (x)^2 - (x-1)^2 = 2x - 1, largest differences yield the greatest square decrease. Use a frequency bucket count[d] over bounded differences (<= 10^5) to step down from maxDiff in O(N + M) time.

title: Minimum Insertions to Balance a Parentheses String
summary: Find minimum insertions required to balance parentheses where each '(' requires two consecutive '))'.
approach: Greedy linear traversal maintaining count of unmatched '(' and required insertions. Consecutive ')' are grouped together, inserting missing ')' or '(' when necessary.

title: Remove Outermost Parentheses
summary: Remove the outermost parentheses of every primitive substring in a valid parentheses string.
approach: Track nesting depth linearly. Only include '(' when current depth > 0 before incrementing, and include ')' when depth > 0 after decrementing.

title: Remove Invalid Parentheses
summary: Remove the minimum number of invalid parentheses to make the input string valid, returning all unique results.
approach: Precompute misplaced '(' and ')' counts to bound search depth. Use DFS backtracking with adjacent duplicate pruning and validity checking.
timeComplexity: O(2^N) bounded by O(C(N, rem) * N)

title: Minimum Add to Make Parentheses Valid
summary: Determine the minimum number of parentheses additions needed to make a string of parentheses valid.
approach: Greedy linear scan counting unmatched open parentheses and insertions required for unmatched closing parentheses in O(N) time and O(1) space.

title: Score of Parentheses
summary: Calculate the numerical score of a balanced parentheses string according to compounding nesting rules.
approach: Track nesting depth linearly. Each immediate '()' pair contributes 2^depth (1 << depth) to the total score in O(N) time and O(1) space.

title: Valid Parenthesis String
summary: Check whether a string with '(', ')' and wildcard '*' can represent a valid balanced parentheses sequence.
approach: Greedy range tracking maintaining minimum and maximum possible open parentheses count [lo, hi]. If hi < 0 at any point return false; return lo == 0 at the end.

title: Longest Valid Parentheses
summary: Find the length of the longest valid parentheses substring in a given string of parentheses.
approach: Index-based stack tracking with base boundary at -1. Pop on ')' and either update maximum substring length (i - stack[top]) or set new barrier index.

title: Generate Parentheses
summary: Generate all combinations of well-formed parentheses given n pairs.
approach: Backtracking ensuring valid prefix invariants: only add '(' if open < n, and only add ')' if close < open.
timeComplexity: O(4^n / sqrt(n)) bounded by n-th Catalan number

title: Valid Parentheses
summary: Determine if an input string with brackets '()', '{}', and '[]' is valid.
approach: Parity check length, then use a primitive character stack to match closing brackets with opening brackets.

title: Maximum Nesting Depth of Two Valid Parentheses Strings
summary: Split a VPS into two disjoint VPS subsequences A and B to minimize max(depth(A), depth(B)).
approach: Assign parentheses based on the parity of their nesting depth (depth % 2) so that alternating nesting levels are distributed evenly between the two subsequences.

title: Check if There Is a Valid Parentheses String Path
summary: Check if there is a path from (0, 0) to (m - 1, n - 1) in a grid of '(' and ')' that forms a valid balanced parentheses string.
approach: Prune early if path length is odd or boundary brackets are invalid. Use 3D Dynamic Programming dp[i][j][b] tracking reachability of open parentheses balance b at cell (i, j).

title: Maximum Nesting Depth of the Parentheses
summary: Return the maximum nesting depth of parentheses in a valid parentheses string s.
approach: Scan through the string using a depth counter: increment on '(' updating maxDepth, and decrement on ')'.

title: Reverse Substrings Between Each Pair of Parentheses
summary: Reverse the strings in each pair of matching parentheses, starting from the innermost one, returning the bracket-free resulting string.
approach: Maintain a stack of string buffers representing enclosing scopes. When encountering '(', push the current buffer and start anew. When encountering ')', reverse the current buffer, pop the outer buffer, and append to it.

title: Evaluate the Bracket Pairs of a String
summary: Replace bracketed keys in a string with their corresponding values from a knowledge dictionary, or '?' if the key is not present.
approach: Populate a hash map with knowledge key-value pairs, then linearly parse the string replacing each bracketed (key) with map lookup or '?' otherwise appending characters directly.

title: Brace Expansion II
summary: Evaluate an expression consisting of curly braces, commas, and lowercase letters representing sets of words under union and concatenation grammar rules.
approach: Recursive descent parser where parse() computes the Cartesian concatenation product of adjacent sub-expressions until a comma or closing brace, and parseSingle() handles union sets inside curly braces separated by commas.

title: Smallest Index With Digit Sum Equal to Index
summary: Return the smallest index i in nums such that the sum of the digits of nums[i] equals i.
approach: Iterate sequentially from index 0 to n - 1, compute the digit sum of each element by extracting digits modulo 10, and return the first matching index.

title: Minimum Operations to Reduce X to Zero
summary: Find the minimum number of operations to remove elements from either end summing to x by finding the longest central contiguous subarray summing to total - x.
approach: Invert the problem to find the maximum length contiguous subarray summing to total - x using a two-pointer sliding window, leveraging the positivity of array elements for strict monotonicity.

title: Find X Value of Array II
summary: Process persistent point updates and count the number of non-empty prefixes of a query suffix whose product modulo k equals x.
approach: Build a segment tree where each node maintains total product modulo k and a frequency array of prefix remainder products, merge children by scaling right prefixes by left product, apply point updates, and query the suffix range [start, n - 1].
timeComplexity: O(N * k + Q * k * log N)

title: Find X Value of Array I
summary: Count the number of contiguous non-empty subarrays whose element product modulo k equals x for each x from 0 to k - 1.
approach: Maintain a DP frequency array tracking remainder counts of subarrays ending at the previous position, transition each remainder by multiplying with (nums[r] % k) modulo k, include the single-element subarray nums[r], and accumulate into the result array.

title: Reverse Degree of a String
summary: Calculate the reverse degree of a string by summing the product of each character's reversed alphabet position and its 1-indexed string position.
approach: Iterate through each character, compute its reversed alphabet position (26 - (ch - 'a')), multiply by (index + 1), and sum the results.

title: Circle and Rectangle Overlapping
summary: Determine if an axis-aligned rectangle and a circle have at least one common overlapping point.
approach: Find the closest point on the rectangle to the circle's center by clamping the coordinates, then verify if the squared Euclidean distance is within radius squared.

title: Maximum Number of Non-Overlapping Substrings
summary: Find the maximum number of non-overlapping substrings such that every character in each substring appears solely within that substring, minimizing total length.
approach: Precompute first and last occurrences of all 26 characters. For each valid starting character, expand candidate windows and select non-overlapping intervals greedily, replacing longer outer intervals with strictly contained shorter ones.

title: Find Two Non-overlapping Sub-arrays Each With Target Sum
summary: Find two non-overlapping subarrays each summing to target such that the sum of their lengths is minimized.
approach: Use prefix sums and a hash map to detect subarrays summing to target, paired with a prefix DP array storing the minimum length of any preceding valid subarray.

title: Number of Sets of K Non-Overlapping Line Segments
summary: Calculate the number of ways to draw k non-overlapping line segments that may share endpoints using a combinatorial bijection to binomial coefficient.
approach: By mapping shared boundary points through coordinate expansion, the problem is equivalent to choosing 2k points out of n + k - 1 points. Computed using Pascal's triangle DP modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Maximum Number of Non-overlapping Palindrome Substrings
summary: Find the maximum count of non-overlapping palindrome substrings of length at least k using dynamic programming precomputation and greedy interval selection.
approach: Precompute all palindrome substrings using an O(N²) DP table. Then greedily pick the earliest non-overlapping palindromes of minimal valid length (k or k+1).

title: Rectangle Overlap
summary: Determine whether two axis-aligned rectangles have an intersection with positive area.
approach: Check the complementary condition where rec2 is entirely to the right, left, above, or below rec1. Return the negation of this disjunction.

title: Image Overlap
summary: Calculate the maximum possible overlap of 1 bits between two binary images by testing all horizontal and vertical translation shifts.
approach: Iterate through all (2n - 1) * (2n - 1) possible shift vectors (dx, dy). For each shift, count overlapping 1s within valid matrix boundaries and take the maximum.

title: Maximum Score of Non-overlapping Intervals
summary: Find the lexicographically smallest sorted list of up to 4 non-overlapping intervals yielding maximum total weight using interval sorting, binary search, and prefix DP.
approach: Sort intervals by right endpoint. For each interval, binary search for the rightmost non-overlapping preceding interval. Maintain prefix DP tables for choosing up to 4 intervals with tie-breaking for lexicographically smaller index combinations.

title: Unique 3-Digit Even Numbers
summary: Determine the number of distinct three-digit even numbers with no leading zeros that can be formed from an array of digits using permutations and set deduplication.
approach: Iterate through all unique index triplets (i, j, k) with distinct indices. Verify that digits[i] != 0 and digits[k] is even. Add the resulting 3-digit number to a set to remove duplicates, returning the set size.

title: Count Nodes Equal to Average of Subtree
summary: Return the number of nodes in a binary tree where the node's value equals the integer average of the values in its subtree using post-order DFS.
approach: Perform a bottom-up post-order DFS where each recursive call returns the subtree sum and subtree node count. Compute the integer average at each node and increment the count if it matches the node's value.

title: Count Commas in Range II
summary: Calculate the total number of commas used in standard number formatting for integers up to 10^15 using 64-bit threshold scaling.
approach: Iterate through powers of 1,000 using 64-bit integers and add (n - threshold + 1) for each threshold level until the threshold exceeds n.

title: Count Commas in Range
summary: Count the total number of commas used in standard number formatting for all integers from 1 to n by summing threshold tier contributions.
approach: Iteratively add (n - threshold + 1) for each comma threshold starting from 1,000 and scaling by 1,000 each step until the threshold exceeds n.

title: Distinct Subsequences II
summary: Calculate the number of distinct non-empty subsequences of a string modulo 10^9 + 7 using dynamic programming tracked by the last character of each subsequence.
approach: Maintain dp[c] representing distinct subsequences ending with character c. For each character ch, compute total = 1 + sum(dp) modulo 10^9 + 7, then set dp[ch - 'a'] = total. The final answer is sum(dp) modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Distinct Subsequences
summary: Calculate the number of distinct subsequences of string s that match target string t using a 2D dynamic programming grid.
approach: Define dp[i][j] as the number of distinct subsequences of prefix s[0..i-1] equal to t[0..j-1]. Transition using dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] + (s[i-1] == t[j-1] ? dp[i-1][j-1] : 0) with base case dp[i][0] = 1.

title: Smallest Stable Index II
summary: Find the smallest index i such that the instability score max(nums[0..i]) - min(nums[i..n-1]) is less than or equal to k for arrays up to 10^5 elements using prefix maximum and suffix minimum arrays.
approach: Precompute prefix maximums and suffix minimums across nums in O(N). Traverse index i from 0 to n-1 and return the first index where prefixMax[i] - suffixMin[i] <= k. Return -1 if no such index exists.

title: Smallest Stable Index I
summary: Find the smallest index i such that the instability score, defined as max(nums[0..i]) - min(nums[i..n-1]), is less than or equal to k using prefix maximum and suffix minimum arrays.
approach: Precompute prefix maximums and suffix minimums across the array in O(N). Iterate through each index i from 0 to n-1 and return the first index where prefixMax[i] - suffixMin[i] <= k. Return -1 if no such index exists.

title: Construct Uniform Parity Array II
summary: Determine if an array nums1 can be converted to an all-even or all-odd array nums2 by optionally subtracting a strictly smaller element of appropriate parity.
approach: Evaluate target parities 0 and 1. If an element does not match target parity, verify that a strictly smaller element of needed parity exists by checking against the global minimum of that parity.

title: Construct Uniform Parity Array I
summary: Determine if an array nums1 can be converted to an all-even or all-odd array nums2 by choosing to keep elements or subtract another element using parity analysis.
approach: Count even and odd elements. All even is possible if oddCount == 0 or oddCount >= 2. All odd is possible if evenCount == 0 or oddCount >= 1. Return allEven || allOdd.

title: Minimum Moves to Clean the Classroom
summary: Find the minimum moves required for a student to collect all litter items in an m x n classroom using energy replenishment areas and obstacles via BFS with bitmask state tracking.
approach: Model the search as a shortest-path problem on a multi-dimensional state graph (r, c, energy, litterMask). Use Breadth-First Search (BFS) starting from S with full energy. When stepping onto R, restore energy to maximum capacity. When stepping onto a litter cell L, flip its corresponding bit in the bitmask. The first state reaching fullMask yields the minimum moves.

title: Find the Minimum and Maximum Number of Nodes Between Critical Points
summary: Find the minimum and maximum distance between critical points (local maxima and minima) in a singly linked list.
approach: Traverse the linked list to find 1-based indices of all critical points. If there are fewer than two, return [-1, -1]. Compute the maximum distance as the difference between the first and last critical point, and find the minimum distance by checking adjacent critical point pairs.

title: Removing Minimum and Maximum From Array
summary: Find the minimum number of deletions from the front and/or back of an array to remove both the minimum and maximum elements.
approach: Identify the indices of the minimum and maximum elements. Compare the cost of three candidate deletion strategies: deleting both from the front, deleting both from the back, or deleting each from opposite ends.

title: Make Lexicographically Smallest Array by Swapping Elements
summary: Rearrange an array into its lexicographically smallest permutation by swapping elements differing by at most limit.
approach: Sort array indices by their values, partition consecutive elements differing by at most limit into connected component groups, sort the indices within each group, and place sorted values back into sorted index positions.

title: Lexicographically Smallest Palindromic Permutation Greater Than Target
summary: Find the lexicographically smallest palindromic permutation of s that is strictly greater than target.
approach: Validate palindrome feasibility, halve the character pool to construct the left half, and greedily explore matching the target prefix while branching with the smallest strictly greater character and filling the remainder in ascending order.

title: Lexicographically Smallest Permutation Greater Than Target
summary: Find the lexicographically smallest permutation of s that is strictly greater than target.
approach: Scan from left to right to find the rightmost breakpoint where an unused character greater than target[i] is available while matching target prefix. At this breakpoint, pick the smallest strictly greater character, and sort all remaining characters in ascending order.

title: Shortest and Lexicographically Smallest Beautiful String
summary: Find the shortest substring with exactly k ones, breaking ties by lexicographically smallest order.
approach: Use a sliding window tracking the count of ones; dynamically trim excess ones and leading zeros to maintain minimal window length and compare candidates lexicographically.

title: Smallest Missing Multiple of K
summary: Find the smallest positive multiple of k that does not appear in the given integer array nums.
approach: Insert all elements of nums into a hash set for O(1) membership lookup, then iteratively check multiples k, 2k, 3k... and return the first one missing from the set.

title: Stone Game VIII
summary: Find the maximum score difference Alice can achieve by removing stones, scoring their prefix sum, and replacing them with a single merged stone.
approach: Prefix sums are invariant under stone merges. Using backward dynamic programming, each state computes dp = max(dp, prefix[i] - dp) to determine the optimal score difference in linear time.

title: Sum Game
summary: Determine if Alice can guarantee unequal digit sums across both halves of an even-length string with wildcard question marks.
approach: Alice always wins if total question marks are odd. When even, Bob can pair question mark plays to force sums of 9; Bob wins if and only if known sum difference perfectly counters the question mark disparity.

title: Check Divisibility by Digit Sum and Product
summary: Determine whether a given positive integer n is divisible by the sum of its digit sum and digit product.
approach: Extract digits of n sequentially to accumulate digit sum and digit product. Check if n is divisible by the combined sum.

title: Kth Smallest Amount With Single Denomination Combination
summary: Find the k-th smallest amount that can be formed as a multiple of any single coin denomination using binary search and the Principle of Inclusion-Exclusion.
approach: Binary search on the answer in range [1, k * min(coins)]. For a candidate amount x, count numbers <= x divisible by at least one coin denomination using bitmask inclusion-exclusion over coin LCMs.

title: Distribute Elements Into Two Arrays I
summary: Distribute elements of an array into two arrays based on which array currently has the greater last element, and return their concatenation.
approach: Direct simulation by initializing arr1 with nums[0] and arr2 with nums[1]. For subsequent elements, append to arr1 if its last element exceeds arr2's last element, else append to arr2. Return arr1 concatenated with arr2.

title: Cinema Seat Allocation
summary: Determine the maximum number of 4-person family groups that can be seated across an n-row cinema with reserved seats.
approach: Represent reserved seats per row as a bitmask in a hash map. For reserved rows, greedily check disjoint 4-seat candidate blocks [2-5] and [6-9], falling back to [4-7]. Add 2 families for every unreserved row.

title: Find the Largest Almost Missing Integer
summary: Find the largest integer that appears in exactly one contiguous subarray of length k within nums.
approach: Iterate through each subarray of size k, mark unique values in each window, and track subarray appearance counts in a frequency table. Return the maximum value whose count equals 1.

title: Stone Game V
summary: Find the maximum score Alice can achieve in Stone Game V by dividing rows into two non-empty segments where the higher sum is discarded.
approach: Use interval dynamic programming with memoization memo[l][r]. Precompute prefix sums for O(1) interval sum queries. For each partition point m from l to r - 1, compare leftSum and rightSum: keep the segment with smaller sum, or choose the optimal if sums are equal.

title: Stone Game IX
summary: Determine whether Alice can force a win in an optimal turn-based stone removal game avoiding running sums divisible by 3.
approach: Classify stones by remainder modulo 3. Stones with remainder 0 toggle parity without altering modulo state. Analyze whether Alice can guarantee alternating moves without reaching a multiple of 3 based on 0-stone parity.

title: Longest Subsequence With Non-Zero Bitwise XOR
summary: Find the maximum length of a subsequence whose bitwise XOR sum is non-zero.
approach: Compute the total XOR sum. If non-zero, the entire array of length N is valid. If zero, removing any single non-zero element yields a non-zero XOR sum of length N - 1; otherwise, return 0 if all elements are zero.

title: Maximum Length Substring With Two Occurrences
summary: Find the length of the longest substring containing at most two occurrences of each character using a sliding window.
approach: Track character frequencies within the active window using a 26-element array. Expand the right pointer, and shrink the window from the left whenever any character frequency exceeds 2.

title: Longest Substring of One Repeating Character
summary: Process dynamic point updates on a string and return the maximum length of a repeating character substring after each update.
approach: Build a segment tree maintaining boundary characters, longest prefix/suffix of identical characters, and the best repeating substring. Combine child intervals across mid boundaries in O(1) per pull and handle updates in O(log N).

title: Length of Longest Subarray With at Most K Frequency
summary: Find the length of the longest contiguous subarray where no element appears more than k times using a sliding window.
approach: Expand the right pointer while maintaining element frequencies in a hash map. When any frequency exceeds k, advance the left pointer until validity is restored.

title: Smallest Missing Integer Greater Than Sequential Prefix Sum
summary: Find the smallest integer missing from an array that is greater than or equal to the sum of its longest sequential prefix starting at index 0.
approach: Sum the longest sequential prefix where nums[i] == nums[i - 1] + 1, store all elements in a hash set, and increment the sum until finding a value absent from the set.

title: Stone Game IV
summary: Determine if Alice can win the stone game by repeatedly removing any non-zero square number of stones until no moves remain.
approach: Impartial game DP: a position i is winning if there exists some perfect square k^2 <= i such that i - k^2 is a losing position for the opponent.

title: Stone Game II
summary: Find the maximum number of stones Alice can collect when both players take turns choosing between 1 and 2M piles and update M = max(M, X).
approach: Compute suffix sums of piles to determine remaining stones from any index. Use top-down dynamic programming with memoization on state (i, M) where taking X piles (1 <= X <= 2M) leaves the opponent with solve(i + X, max(M, X)), maximizing suffixSum[i] - opponentGets.

title: Find the Lexicographically Smallest Valid Sequence
summary: Find the lexicographically smallest sequence of indices in word1 forming a subsequence almost equal to word2 (with at most one character changed).
approach: Precompute the latest valid suffix matching positions in word1 using a backward two-pointer pass. Then make a forward greedy pass through word1, matching characters identically when possible, or consuming the single allowed mismatch when the remaining suffix of word2 can still be matched in the remainder of word1.

title: Smallest Divisible Digit Product II
summary: Find the smallest zero-free number greater than or equal to num whose digit product is divisible by t.
approach: Factorize t into prime factors 2, 3, 5, 7 (returning -1 if any larger prime factor exists). Greedily decompose factors into minimal digits (8, 9, 4, 6, 2, 3, 5, 7). Iterate right-to-left across valid zero-free prefixes to find the first position that can be incremented while fitting remaining required digits in the suffix, or extend the number length by prepending '1's.

title: Smallest Divisible Digit Product I
summary: Find the smallest number greater than or equal to n whose digit product is divisible by t.
approach: Iterate upwards starting from n and compute the digit product of each candidate integer. Return the first number whose digit product is divisible by t. Within at most 10 iterations, a multiple of 10 is reached (digit product 0), guaranteeing O(1) termination.

title: Remove Methods From Project
summary: Remove a buggy method and all methods reachable from it, provided no non-suspicious method invokes any suspicious method.
approach: Traverse the directed invocation graph starting from method k using BFS to discover all suspicious methods. Then check all invocations: if any non-suspicious method calls a suspicious method, abort and return all methods; otherwise, return all non-suspicious methods.

title: Find Missing Elements
summary: Find all missing integers between the minimum and maximum elements of a unique integer array.
approach: Find the minimum and maximum elements in nums, insert all elements into a hash set for O(1) membership testing, and collect all integers from min to max absent from the set into a sorted result list.

title: Stone Game III
summary: Determine the winner (Alice, Bob, or Tie) of a turn-based game where players take 1, 2, or 3 stones from the remaining row to maximize relative score advantage.
approach: Use linear Dynamic Programming dp[i] from right to left tracking the maximum score difference (current player - opponent) achievable from stoneValue[i..n-1] by evaluating choices k in {1, 2, 3}.

title: Stone Game
summary: Determine if Alice wins a stone-picking game where players take piles from either end of an even-length array with an odd total sum of stones.
approach: Use interval Dynamic Programming dp[i][j] tracking the maximum relative stone advantage the current player can achieve over their opponent from piles[i..j]. Alternatively, Alice always wins (return true) because with an even number of piles and odd total sum, Alice can strictly force picking either all even or all odd indices.

title: Predict the Winner
summary: Determine if Player 1 can win or tie in an optimal two-player zero-sum game picking numbers from either end of an array.
approach: Use interval Dynamic Programming dp[i][j] tracking the maximum relative score difference achievable by the current player from subarray nums[i..j].

title: Minimum Number of Pushes to Type Word II
summary: Find the minimum number of key pushes needed to type a word on a remappable 8-key telephone keypad.
approach: Count the frequency of each character, sort frequencies in descending order, and greedily place the most frequent characters in the earliest available push depths (each depth holds 8 keys).

title: Minimum Number of Pushes to Type Word I
summary: Find the minimum number of key pushes needed to type a string of distinct characters on a remappable 8-key keypad.
approach: Greedily distribute characters across the 8 keys so that each character is assigned the minimum available push depth. For character index i, pushes equal (i / 8) + 1.

title: Smallest Palindromic Rearrangement II
summary: Find the k-th lexicographically smallest distinct palindromic permutation of a given palindromic string s.
approach: Reduce the problem to determining the first half using multinomial permutations with repetition. For each position, greedily test characters in alphabetical order, subtract counts when skipped, and cap combination calculations at 2,000,000 to prevent overflow.

title: Smallest Palindromic Rearrangement I
summary: Rearrange the characters of a given palindromic string s to form the lexicographically smallest palindrome.
approach: Count character frequencies across all 26 lowercase English letters. Greedily append pairs of characters in alphabetical order to the left half, place the unique odd character (if any) at the center, and append the reversed left half to form the final palindrome.

title: Maximum Product of Two Elements in an Array
summary: Choose two different indices i and j of an integer array to maximize (nums[i] - 1) * (nums[j] - 1).
approach: Track the two largest elements in nums (max1 and max2) during a single pass and return (max1 - 1) * (max2 - 1).

title: Maximum Product of Three Numbers
summary: Find three numbers in an integer array whose product is maximum, and return the maximum product.
approach: Single-pass linear scan to track the three largest elements (max1, max2, max3) and two smallest elements (min1, min2). Return max(max1 * max2 * max3, max1 * min1 * min2).

title: Maximum Product of Two Digits
summary: Return the maximum product of any two digits in a positive integer n.
approach: Extract digits of n and greedily track the top two largest digits seen so far (first and second). Return first * second.

title: Number of Unique XOR Triplets II
summary: Calculate the number of unique XOR triplet values formed by taking three elements from nums where indices satisfy i <= j <= k.
approach: Model the multiset selection of 3 elements using a bounded DP table dp[k][v] of size 4 x 2048. For each element x, allow choosing it up to 3 times via reverse knapsack transitions, then count reachable XOR values in dp[3].

title: Number of Unique XOR Triplets I
summary: Determine the number of unique XOR triplet values possible by taking the XOR sum of three elements from a permutation of numbers 1 to n.
approach: Analyze cases: for n=1 return 1, for n=2 return 2. For n >= 3, all numbers from 0 up to the next power of 2 minus 1 are formable; compute the smallest power of 2 strictly greater than n.

title: Maximize Active Section with Trade II
summary: Process range queries on a binary string to find the maximum possible active sections after performing at most one trade that merges adjacent 0-blocks inside each query range.
approach: Run-length encode the string to identify candidate 1-blocks flanked by 0-blocks. For each query [l, r], binary search finds candidate ranges; query internal candidates via Sparse Table (RMQ) in O(1) and evaluate partially clipped boundaries.

title: Maximize Active Section with Trade I
summary: Maximize the count of active sections in a binary string by executing at most one trade that clears a block of 1s between two 0 blocks and flips the resulting merged block to 1s.
approach: Scan the string to count total 1s and group consecutive runs of identical characters. Whenever two 0-blocks are separated by a 1-block, trading the intermediate 1-block enables merging both 0-blocks, adding L1 + L2 active sections.

title: Shift 2D Grid
summary: Shift a 2D grid of size m x n by k steps cyclicly according to the given transformation rules.
approach: Flatten the 2D grid concept into 1D indices [0..m*n-1], apply modulo shift (idx + k) % (m * n), and map the new 1D index back to 2D coordinates (newIdx / n, newIdx % n).

title: Smallest Subsequence of Distinct Characters
summary: Return the lexicographically smallest subsequence of a string containing all distinct characters exactly once.
approach: Precompute the last occurrence index of each character. Traverse the string while using a monotonic stack and a visited boolean array, greedily popping characters larger than the current character if they appear again later.

title: Find Greatest Common Divisor of Array
summary: Find the greatest common divisor of the minimum and maximum numbers in an array.
approach: Scan the array in a single pass to find the minimum and maximum elements, then compute and return their GCD using the Euclidean algorithm.

title: Sorted GCD Pair Queries
summary: Find the GCD of all pairs, sort them ascending, and answer queries asking for the k-th smallest GCD pair.
approach: Count multiples for each divisor g in O(M log M) to calculate total pairs divisible by g. Use backwards sieve-like inclusion-exclusion to determine exact GCD frequencies. Build prefix sums and answer each query using binary search in O(log M).
timeComplexity: O(N + M log M + Q log M)

title: Sum of GCD of Formed Pairs
summary: Compute prefix GCDs with running maximums, sort the resulting array, and find the sum of GCDs of symmetric pairs using two pointers.
approach: Iterate through nums maintaining running maximum mx and compute prefixGcd[i] = gcd(nums[i], mx). Sort prefixGcd in non-decreasing order and pair the l-th and r-th elements inward using two pointers, accumulating their GCD.

title: GCD of Odd and Even Sums
summary: Compute the greatest common divisor of the sum of the first n positive odd numbers and the sum of the first n positive even numbers.
approach: The sum of the first n odd numbers is n^2 and the sum of the first n even numbers is n(n + 1). Since gcd(n^2, n(n + 1)) = n * gcd(n, n + 1) and consecutive integers are coprime, the result is always n.

title: Find the Number of Subsequences With Equal GCD
summary: Find the number of pairs of disjoint non-empty subsequences of nums that have equal GCD modulo 10^9 + 7.
approach: Maintain 2D DP table tracking running GCD pairs (g1, g2) for both subsequences. For each element, either skip it or update g1 or g2 via gcd. Sum dp[g][g] for all g >= 1.

title: Sequential Digits
summary: Find all numbers within a given range [low, high] whose digits are strictly sequential and increasing.
approach: Use a queue seeded with digits 1 through 9. Incrementally append the next sequential digit (lastDigit + 1) while the number remains within range, then sort the results.

title: Rank Transform of an Array
summary: Replace each element in an array with its 1-based rank, where larger elements receive larger ranks and equal elements share the same rank.
approach: Sort a copy of the array and map each distinct value to its 1-based rank using a Hash Map. Then replace elements in the original array with their corresponding ranks.

title: Count the Number of Complete Components
summary: Count the number of connected components in an undirected graph where every vertex has an edge to every other vertex in its component.
approach: Traverse each connected component using Breadth-First Search (BFS) to gather all vertices. A component with k vertices is complete if and only if every vertex in it has a degree of exactly k - 1.

title: Path Existence Queries in a Graph II
summary: Find the minimum distance between pairs of nodes in an unweighted undirected graph where edges connect nodes with absolute value difference at most maxDiff.
approach: Sort nodes by value and use a two-pointer scan to identify the greedy furthest jump. Build a binary lifting table to answer shortest path queries in O(log N) time.

title: Path Existence Queries in a Graph I
summary: Determine whether paths exist between pairs of nodes in an undirected graph where edges connect nodes whose values differ by at most maxDiff.
approach: Utilize the non-decreasing order of nums: whenever nums[i] - nums[i - 1] > maxDiff, a new connected component begins. Answer queries in O(1) by checking component equivalence.

title: Concatenate Non-Zero Digits and Multiply by Sum II
summary: Process range queries on a digit string to extract non-zero digits, form concatenated values modulo 10^9 + 7, and multiply by their digit sums.
approach: Build a Segment Tree or use Prefix Arrays with modular arithmetic and powers of 10 to evaluate range concatenated values and digit sums efficiently.
timeComplexity: O(N + Q log N) or O(N + Q)

title: Concatenate Non-Zero Digits and Multiply by Sum I
summary: Concatenate all non-zero digits of an integer n into a new integer x and return x multiplied by the sum of its digits.
approach: Iterate through the digits of n, filtering out zeroes to construct x while concurrently accumulating the digit sum.

title: Remove Covered Intervals
summary: Remove all intervals that are covered by another interval in the list and return the count of remaining intervals.
approach: Sort intervals by start ascending and end descending, then greedily count intervals whose end exceeds the maximum end seen so far.

title: Number of Paths with Max Score
summary: Find the maximum sum of numeric characters and number of paths modulo 10^9 + 7 to reach E from S on a grid with obstacles.
approach: Use bottom-up dynamic programming from (n-1, n-1) to (0, 0) simultaneously tracking maximum path scores and counts of optimal paths.

title: Minimum Score of a Path Between Two Cities
summary: Find the minimum score (minimum edge distance) among all roads in a connected component containing city 1 and city n.
approach: Traverse the connected component containing city 1 using Breadth-First Search (BFS), tracking the minimum distance across all explored edges.

title: Network Recovery Pathways
summary: Find the maximum path score (minimum edge cost) among all valid paths from 0 to n - 1 in a DAG within total budget k.
approach: Binary search on the minimum edge weight threshold and verify reachability within total cost k using DAG topological shortest path.

title: Find a Safe Walk Through a Grid
summary: Determine if there exists a walk from (0, 0) to (m - 1, n - 1) in a binary grid such that remaining health stays at least 1.
approach: Use modified Dijkstra algorithm with a max-heap tracking the maximum health achievable upon entering each cell.

title: Find the Safest Path in a Grid
summary: Find the maximum safeness factor of all paths from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell in a grid containing thieves.
approach: Run multi-source BFS from all thieves to compute the distance transform matrix, then binary search on the minimum safeness factor using BFS reachability.

title: Number of Ways to Assign Edge Weights I
summary: Find the maximum depth D from root node 1 to any node x in an undirected tree, then compute the number of edge weight assignments on that path yielding an odd total cost.
approach: Run BFS from root node 1 to find the maximum depth D. On any path of length D, each of the first D - 1 edges can be assigned weight 1 or 2 arbitrarily (2^(D - 1) ways), while the final edge has exactly one choice that guarantees an odd sum. Hence, return 2^(D - 1) % (10^9 + 7).

title: Maximum Total Subarray Value II
summary: Choose exactly k distinct non-empty subarrays to maximize the sum of max - min values without repeating identical subarrays.
approach: Precompute static RMQ with Sparse Table in O(N log N). Push the longest candidate (l, n - 1) for each left index l into a max-heap. Pop top k times, adding value to answer and pushing the predecessor range (l, r - 1).

title: Maximum Total Subarray Value I
summary: Choose exactly k non-empty subarrays to maximize the sum of max - min values, allowing repeated selection.
approach: Any chosen subarray's value is at most max(nums) - min(nums). Since duplicate subarray selection is permitted, choose the subarray containing both extremes all k times, giving (max - min) * k in O(N) time and O(1) space.

title: Partition Array According to Given Pivot
summary: Rearrange array such that elements less than pivot come first, followed by pivot elements, then elements greater than pivot, maintaining relative ordering.
approach: Perform three linear passes over nums to preserve stability: first append elements less than pivot, second append elements equal to pivot, and third append elements greater than pivot.

title: Create Binary Tree From Descriptions
summary: Construct a binary tree from parent-child-isLeft descriptions and return its root.
approach: Use a hash map to instantiate and look up tree nodes by value, establishing parent-child links. Concurrently record all child node values in a hash set. The tree root is the unique parent that never appears in the children set.

title: Left and Right Sum Differences
summary: Calculate the difference array answer where answer[i] = |leftSum[i] - rightSum[i]|.
approach: Precompute the total sum of the array. Iterate through each element while maintaining leftSum and rightSum (totalSum - leftSum - nums[i]), assigning answer[i] = |leftSum - rightSum| in O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.

title: Total Waviness of Numbers in Range II
summary: Calculate the sum of peaks and valleys across all digits for each number within an inclusive range up to 10^15 using Digit DP.
approach: Decompose the range via prefix subtraction and use memoized Digit DP tracking position, preceding two digits, accumulated waviness, and tight constraint.

title: Total Waviness of Numbers in Range I
summary: Calculate the sum of peaks and valleys across all digits for each number within an inclusive range.
approach: Iterate through each number in the range, examine its intermediate digits, and increment the waviness count whenever a digit is strictly greater than or strictly less than both of its neighbors.

title: Earliest Finish Time for Land and Water Rides II
summary: Find the minimum completion time to experience one land ride and one water ride under large constraints.
approach: Sort the second category of rides and use binary search combined with prefix minimum durations and suffix minimum opening finish times to find the optimal second ride in O(log M) time.

title: Earliest Finish Time for Land and Water Rides I
summary: Find the minimum completion time to experience one land ride and one water ride in either order.
approach: Enumerate all pairs of land and water rides across both orderings (land then water, and water then land), computing the earliest valid finish time.

title: Minimum Cost of Buying Candies With Discount
summary: Find the minimum cost of buying all candies when every third candy is free if its cost is less than or equal to the two purchased candies.
approach: Sort the candies in descending order and greedily pair the two most expensive candies to take the third most expensive for free.
